q: can you pin point which campaign gave the low intent traffic and which were actually profitables
answer:
Short answer: High-volume, low-intent traffic came mainly from Google demand campaigns (notably "Demand Gen | Hero Products") while the most profitable campaigns were search/Performance Max and a few Meta product campaigns — e.g. "[Google Build] PMax - Seasonal New | 27th May" and "[Google Build] Brand Search | 5th March".

Evidence (Oct 1–13, compared internally)
- Low-intent, high-volume campaigns (many clicks, very low CPC, but small share of net sales)
  - [Google Build] Demand Gen | Hero Products | 20 Apr — 22,119 clicks, CPC ~₹1.79, large click volume but not among top net sales (behaviour of high clicks + low net sales = lower intent).
  - TH-383-SUSPENDER-26SEP-ADV+ (meta) — 4,564 clicks, CPC ~₹12.22, high spend but proportionally less net sales vs other high-AOV campaigns.
- Profitable / high net-sales campaigns (strong net sales per order / higher AOV)
  - [Google Build] PMax - Seasonal New | 27th May — net sales ≈ ₹116,562; orders 65; AOV ≈ ₹2,338.
  - [Google Build] Brand Search | 5th March — net sales ≈ ₹91,976; orders 47; AOV ≈ ₹2,596.
  - TH-336-PAWTECH-26SEP and TH-149-SCRATCHLOUNGE-25SEP (meta) — each delivered >₹60k net sales with healthy AOVs.
- Why this supports your hypothesis
  - Big jump in clicks from demand-gen channels with very low CPCs indicates broader / lower-intent audiences.  
  - Conversion rates by campaign vary; the demand-gen campaign has many clicks but comparatively small net sales/orders, consistent with creative/landing mismatch or traffic intent issues.
  - Several campaigns with higher AOVs and fewer clicks drove most of the profitable sales.

Caveats: metrics came from combined commerce, paid_media and web_sessions parts; some entities are missing from one or more parts so per-campaign comparisons are best when run together for a selected campaign list. Data as of 2026-10-14.

Period: 2026-10-01..2026-10-13 · Currency: INR · Data as of 2026-10-14
